full_explanation: Think of 12 as 4 + 4 + 4. Each 25 × 4 makes 100, and three of them make 300. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Give both numbers two decimal places: 0.70 and 0.65. Now compare 70 and 65.
full_explanation: 0.7 is the same as 0.70, which is 70 hundredths. 0.65 is 65 hundredths. 70 hundredths is more. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Each fraction is one piece away from a whole. A fifth is a smaller piece than a quarter, so 4/5 is closer to 1.
full_explanation: 3/4 is a whole with a quarter missing. 4/5 is a whole with a fifth missing. A fifth is smaller than a quarter, so less is missing from 4/5. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: 50% means half and 25% means a quarter. Half of 36 is 18, and a quarter of 80 is 20.
full_explanation: 50% of 36 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18. 25% of 80 = 80 ÷ 4 = 20. 20 is more than 18. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Find the biggest multiple of 5 that fits into 37: that is 35. Then 37 − 35 = 2 is left over.
full_explanation: 5 × 7 = 35, and 37 is 2 more than 35. The 2 that is left over is the remainder. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

quantity_a: \text{the perimeter of a square with side } 6
quantity_b: \text{the area of a square with side } 4
shortcut_explanation: Perimeter adds the 4 sides: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24. Area multiplies side by side: 4 × 4 = 16.
full_explanation: The perimeter is the distance all the way round: 4 × 6 = 24. The area is the space inside: 4 × 4 = 16. 24 is more than 16. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Keep doubling: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. That is 2⁵, and 32 × 32 = 1024.
full_explanation: 2¹⁰ means ten 2s multiplied together. Five 2s make 32, and the other five make another 32. 32 × 32 = 1024, which is just over 1000. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Multiply before you add, unless brackets say otherwise. So A is 2 + 12 = 14, and B is 5 × 4 = 20.
full_explanation: A has no brackets, so do 3 × 4 = 12 first, then add 2 to get 14. In B the brackets go first: 2 + 3 = 5, then 5 × 4 = 20. 20 is more than 14. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Work out each root first. √16 = 4 and √9 = 3, so B is 7, but √25 is only 5.
full_explanation: √25 = 5, because 5 × 5 = 25. √16 = 4 and √9 = 3, so B is 4 + 3 = 7. Watch out: adding two roots is not the same as the root of the total. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Don't add the tops and the bottoms. 1/3 on its own is already more than 2/7, and A adds 1/4 on top.
full_explanation: 1/3 is the same as 2/6. 2/7 is less than 2/6, because sevenths are smaller pieces than sixths. So 1/3 alone beats 2/7, and A is even bigger. (The exact sum is 7/12.) So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes things smaller. 0.3 × 0.3 is only 0.09.
full_explanation: 0.3 × 0.3 means 3 tenths of 0.3, which is 0.09. 0.09 is much less than 0.3. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Absolute value means how far a number is from 0. 3 − 10 = −7, and −7 is 7 steps from 0.
full_explanation: |−7| = 7. For B, first work out 3 − 10 = −7, then |−7| = 7. Both are 7. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

condition: \text{a class of } 28 \text{ has boys and girls in the ratio } 3 : 4
shortcut_explanation: 3 + 4 = 7 equal groups make the 28 children, so each group is 4. Boys are 3 groups: 3 × 4 = 12.
full_explanation: Split the class into 7 equal groups: 28 ÷ 7 = 4 children in each. Boys get 3 of the groups, so there are 3 × 4 = 12 boys. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Doubling is not the same as squaring. Try x = 1 (2 beats 1), then x = 3 (6 loses to 9).
full_explanation: x + x means 2 times x, and x · x means x times itself. If x = 1, you get 2 and 1, so A wins. If x = 3, you get 6 and 9, so B wins. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: Each pair of −1s makes +1. 100 is even, so it is all pairs: +1. 101 has one −1 left over: −1.
full_explanation: (−1) × (−1) = 1. With 100 copies you get 50 pairs, so the result is 1. With 101 copies, one extra −1 turns it into −1. 1 is more than −1. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Jump to a multiple of 7 just below. 49 is 7 × 7, so 50 leaves 1. 98 is 7 × 14, so 100 leaves 2.
full_explanation: 50 = 49 + 1, and 49 = 7 × 7, so the remainder is 1. 100 = 98 + 2, and 98 = 7 × 14, so the remainder is 2. 2 is more than 1. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the price after a } 10\% \text{ rise and then a } 10\% \text{ fall}
shortcut_explanation: The 10% fall is taken from a bigger price than the 10% rise. So you lose a bit more than you gained.
full_explanation: A 10% rise on 50 adds 5, making 55. A 10% fall on 55 takes away 5.50, leaving 49.50. That is less than 50. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Evenly spaced numbers balance around the middle one. Here the middle number is 4.
full_explanation: Pair them up: 1 and 7, 2 and 6, 3 and 5. Each pair has an average of 4, and the 4 in the middle is 4 too. So the average is 4. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Try x = 2: 1/x is ½, and x is 2. If x is more than 1, then 1/x is less than 1.
full_explanation: 1/x means 1 divided by x. Dividing 1 by a number bigger than 1 gives less than 1. So 1/x is below 1, while x is above 1. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Squaring a number between 0 and 1 makes it smaller. Try x = ½: x² = ¼.
full_explanation: x² means x × x. Multiplying by a number less than 1 leaves you with only part of what you started with. With x = ½, x² = ½ × ½ = ¼, which is smaller. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Try a positive number and a negative one. x = 1 gives 1 + 1 = 2, but x = −1 gives 1 + (−1) = 0.
full_explanation: If x is positive, |x| + x is twice x, which is more than 0. If x is negative, |x| and x cancel out and you get exactly 0. Different numbers give different results. So the answer is D: not enough information.

quantity_a: \text{the remainder when } n^2 + n \text{ is divided by } 2
shortcut_explanation: n² + n is the same as n × (n + 1): two whole numbers next to each other. One of them is always even.
full_explanation: Try n = 3: 3 × 4 = 12, which is even. Try n = 4: 4 × 5 = 20, also even. Of two neighbouring whole numbers, one is even, and even times anything is even. An even number divided by 2 leaves 0. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Try a big number and a fraction. √4 = 2 is less than 4, but √¼ = ½ is more than ¼.
full_explanation: If x = 4, then √x = 2, so B is bigger. If x = ¼, then √x = ½, so A is bigger. For numbers between 0 and 1, the root is bigger than the number. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: a is 5 equal parts and b is 4, but the parts are negative. More negative parts make a smaller number.
full_explanation: Try parts of −1: then a = −5 and b = −4. −4 is bigger than −5. With negative parts, the side with more parts ends up lower. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: An average always lands between the two numbers. b is above a, so the average is above a too.
full_explanation: Try a = 2 and b = 10: the average is 6, which is more than 2. The average sits halfway between a and b, and b is bigger than a. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: (x + 3)² is not x² + 9. It has an extra 6x in the middle, and 6x is positive here.
full_explanation: (x + 3)² means (x + 3) × (x + 3) = x² + 6x + 9. That is x² + 9 with an extra 6x. Since x is positive, 6x is positive too. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Try x = −6: x/2 = −3 and x/3 = −2. For negative numbers, a bigger share is further below 0.
full_explanation: Half of a negative number is a bigger negative piece than a third of it. −3 is less than −2. The same happens for every negative x. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: x doesn't have to be a whole number. x = 2 makes A bigger, but x = ½ makes B bigger.
full_explanation: If x = 2, then x − 1 = 1 and 1 − x = −1, so A wins. If x = ½, then x − 1 = −½ and 1 − x = ½, so B wins. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: The third side must be shorter than the other two put together. 5 + 6 = 11, so x is less than 11.
full_explanation: Sticks of 5 and 6 can only reach 11 if they lie flat in a straight line, and then there is no triangle. So x is less than 11, and 11 is less than 12. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Dividing by 0.5 doubles a number. Doubling makes 3 bigger, but it makes −3 smaller.
full_explanation: x ÷ 0.5 asks how many halves fit into x, and that is twice x. If x = 3, you get 6 and 3, so A wins. If x = −3, you get −6 and −3, so B wins. So the answer is D: not enough information.

condition: \text{two angles of a triangle are } x \text{ and } 90 - x \text{ degrees}
shortcut_explanation: The angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. The first two add up to 90, so the third is 180 − 90 = 90.
full_explanation: x + (90 − x) = 90, so the first two angles add up to 90. All three add up to 180, which leaves 90 for the third angle. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: x² is never negative, and x³ is x² times x. Multiplying by an x below 1 can only make it smaller.
full_explanation: Try x = ½: x² = ¼ and x³ = ⅛. Try x = −2: x² = 4 and x³ = −8. x² wins both times, and it does for every x below 1 except 0. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: The √ sign always gives the positive answer. For a negative x, √(x²) is positive, but x is negative.
full_explanation: Try x = −3: √((−3)²) = √9 = 3, and 3 is more than −3. For any negative x, A is positive and B is negative. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Both squares have an x² and a 1, which cancel out. Only +2x and −2x are left, and together they make 4x.
full_explanation: (x + 1)² = x² + 2x + 1 and (x − 1)² = x² − 2x + 1. Take the second away from the first: the x² and the 1 cancel. What is left is 2x − (−2x) = 4x. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Try 0, then try 3. n = 0 makes them equal, but n = 3 makes n² bigger.
full_explanation: If n = 0, then n² = 0, so the quantities are equal. If n = 3, then n² = 9, which is more than 3. For whole numbers, n² is never less than n, but it can be equal. So the answer is D: not enough information.

quantity_a: x \text{ after a } 20\% \text{ rise and then a } 20\% \text{ fall}
shortcut_explanation: A rise and a fall of the same percent never cancel out. You end up 4% lower.
full_explanation: Try x = 100: a 20% rise makes 120. A 20% fall takes away 24, because that is 20% of 120. That leaves 96, which is less than 100. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: When the signs match, nothing cancels. When they are different, part of each one cancels. Try x = 1, y = 2, then x = 1, y = −2.
full_explanation: If x = 1 and y = 2: |3| = 3 and 1 + 2 = 3, so they are equal. If x = 1 and y = −2: |−1| = 1, but 1 + 2 = 3, so B wins. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: Each fraction is one small piece away from a whole. B is missing a smaller piece, so it is closer to 1.
full_explanation: Try x = 1: A is ½ and B is ⅔, so B is bigger. A is a whole minus 1/(x + 1). B is a whole minus only 1/(2x + 1), which is a smaller piece. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: A ratio doesn't tell you whether the numbers are positive. x = 3, y = 2 makes x bigger; x = −3, y = −2 makes y bigger.
full_explanation: If x = 3 and y = 2, A wins. If x = −3 and y = −2, the ratio is still 3 : 2, but −2 is bigger than −3, so B wins. So the answer is D: not enough information.

quantity_a: \text{the area of a rectangle with perimeter } 20
shortcut_explanation: Don't assume it is a square. A 5 by 5 rectangle has area 25, but a 2 by 8 rectangle has area 16.
full_explanation: A perimeter of 20 means length plus width is 10. A 5 by 5 rectangle has area 25, which is equal. A 2 by 8 rectangle has area 16, which is less. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: A bigger number doesn't always have a bigger square. Try a = 2, b = 1, then try a = 1, b = −3.
full_explanation: If a = 2 and b = 1, the squares are 4 and 1, so A wins. If a = 1 and b = −3, the squares are 1 and 9, so B wins. −3 is far from 0, so its square is big. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: y − x is x − y with the sign flipped. Squaring removes the sign, so both are the same.
full_explanation: Try x = 5 and y = 2: (5 − 2)² = 9 and (2 − 5)² = (−3)² = 9. A number and its opposite always have the same square. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: x⁴ is x² times x². Multiplying a number bigger than 1 by itself makes it bigger.
full_explanation: Try x = 2: x² = 4 and x⁴ = 16. Try x = −3: x² = 9 and x⁴ = 81. Because x² is more than 1, multiplying it by itself always makes it grow. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the remainder when } n^2 \text{ is divided by } 4
shortcut_explanation: Try some odd numbers: 1² = 1, 3² = 9, 5² = 25. Each square is 1 more than a multiple of 4.
full_explanation: Any odd number is 2 times a whole number, plus 1, like 7 = 2 × 3 + 1. Call that whole number k, so the odd number is 2k + 1. Its square is 4k² + 4k + 1, which is 4 × (k² + k), plus 1. So dividing by 4 always leaves 1, for negative odd numbers too. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: a > b doesn't make a/b more than 1 if b is negative. Try a = 2, b = 1, then a = −1, b = −2.
full_explanation: If a = 2 and b = 1, then a/b = 2, which is more than 1. If a = −1 and b = −2, then a/b = ½, which is less than 1. Dividing by a negative number flips the order. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: |x − 3| is how far x is from 3, and |x + 3| is how far x is from −3. A positive x is always closer to 3.
full_explanation: Try x = 1: it is 2 away from 3, but 4 away from −3. Any positive number is on the same side of 0 as 3, so it is nearer to 3. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: a and b add up to 20, so their average is 10. Adding one more 10 can't move an average of 10.
full_explanation: The average of a and b is 20 ÷ 2 = 10. With 10 added, the three numbers add up to 30, and 30 ÷ 3 = 10. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Try a = 9 and b = 16: √25 = 5, but √9 + √16 = 3 + 4 = 7. Splitting a root into two makes it bigger.
full_explanation: Square both sides to compare them. A squared is a + b. B squared is a + b plus an extra 2 × √a × √b, which is positive. So B is bigger. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: The third side must be more than 8 − 5 = 3. So the perimeter is more than 5 + 8 + 3 = 16.
full_explanation: The side of 5 and the third side together must reach past 8, so the third side is more than 3. The perimeter is 5 + 8 + the third side, so it is more than 16. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: x² − 1 is the same as (x − 1) × (x + 1). Divide by x − 1, and x + 1 is left.
full_explanation: Try x = 3: (9 − 1) ÷ 2 = 4, and 3 + 1 = 4. In general, x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1). Because x is not 1, we can divide by x − 1. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.
